options.B: Prevention of unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Elimination of menstrual bleeding and cramping
options.D: Curing existing reproductive tract infections

explanation: Barrier methods physically block sperm while also providing vital protection against STIs, including HIV. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological function of the immune system?

options.A: To regulate blood pressure and cardiac output
options.B: To recognize and protect the body against harmful pathogens and foreign substances
options.C: To produce red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: To digest nutrients in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: The immune system is specifically designed to recognize and defend the body against foreign invaders, toxins, and abnormal cells. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h1)

question: What primary risk is associated with the improper disposal of health care waste regarding healthcare workers?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies
options.B: Needle-stick injuries and blood-borne pathogen transmission
options.C: Respiratory allergies from paper dust
options.D: Musculoskeletal strain from lifting boxes

explanation: Improper disposal of health care waste often leads to needle-stick injuries, which can transmit dangerous blood-borne pathogens such as HIV and Hepatitis B and C to healthcare workers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)
